correctness.rationale: The stipulated alternating bracket gives the free Lie algebra of rank two and class three in every characteristic: the images of x and y fix those of z,u,v by the three defining brackets, and higher brackets vanish in any class-at-most-three target. Its center is Z=span(u,v). For S with image A in L/Z and K=S∩Z, sections are parameterized by q^(dim A(2−dim K)) linear maps f:A→Z/K once a linear lift s is fixed. In general bracket closure requires the central difference [s(a),s(b)]−s([a,b]) modulo K to equal f([a,b]), not merely that the central difference vanish. The actual cases avoid any extra assumption: quotient subalgebras of dimension at most two are abelian, and in dimension three the brackets with lifts of z project to zero and force u,v∈K before any condition involving f is needed. Writing P=q²+q+1, the dimensional contributions for A=0 are (1,q+1,1) in dimensions 0,1,2; the P possible quotient lines contribute Pq²,Pq(q+1),P in dimensions 1,2,3. The q+1 quotient planes all contain the image of z; for direction (a,b) they force K to contain span(au+bv). These give q²(q+1) three-dimensional and q+1 four-dimensional subalgebras. The surjective case yields only L. The plane lifts in dimension three have a one-dimensional central derived algebra with a nonzero alternating bracket on the two generators, so are Heisenberg also in characteristic two. Adding gives all coefficients and the total; the limits are the leading-term ratios. Independent section-map enumeration and direct bracket closure over F₂, F₃ and F₄ returned (1,31,43,19,3,1), (1,121,157,49,4,1), (1,341,421,101,5,1) and abelian three-dimensional counts 7,13,21. value.rationale: This is a full census of a canonical free nilpotent Lie algebra at the first rank-two class with a two-dimensional final central layer. It separates nonabelian from abelian embedded subalgebras and explains why the former dominate the three-dimensional slice, while dimensions one and two dominate the full measure. It is an all-finite-field invariant, including characteristic two, not a small table or a restatement of the ideal enumerator.
